general: Dogs require fresh water available at all times.
Annual vet checkups are recommended for healthy adult dogs; senior dogs (7+) benefit from biannual visits.
Dogs need daily exercise to maintain a healthy weight and mental wellbeing.
Dental hygiene is important — teeth should be brushed at least 3 times per week.
Dogs are social animals and need daily interaction and mental stimulation.
Vaccinations should be kept up to date according to the vet's schedule.
golden retriever: Golden Retrievers need 60–90 minutes of vigorous exercise daily, ideally split into two sessions.
Their dense double coat requires brushing 2–3 times per week to prevent matting and reduce shedding.
They are prone to hip and elbow dysplasia — avoid high-impact jumping in puppies under 18 months.
Goldens love swimming, which is a low-impact exercise great for joint health.
They are prone to obesity — monitor food portions carefully and limit treats.
Monthly ear cleaning is recommended as floppy ears trap moisture and can lead to infections.
labrador: Labradors need 60–80 minutes of exercise daily — they are high-energy and prone to weight gain without it.
Labs are notorious chewers — enrichment toys and chews help prevent destructive behavior.
Their short coat needs brushing once a week; they shed heavily twice a year.
Labs are prone to obesity — measure meals carefully and avoid free feeding.
Regular joint supplements (glucosamine) may be beneficial, especially for senior Labs.
Monthly nail trimming is important as Labs are active but do not always wear down nails naturally.
chihuahua: Chihuahuas need 20–30 minutes of light to moderate exercise per day.
Their small size makes them sensitive to cold — a coat or sweater is recommended in temperatures below 15°C.
Dental hygiene is critical; Chihuahuas are highly prone to dental disease — brush teeth daily if possible.
They can be prone to hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) — feed small meals 2–3 times a day.
Chihuahuas should be protected from rough handling — injuries are more likely due to their small frame.
Despite their size, they need daily socialization and mental enrichment to prevent anxiety.
german shepherd: German Shepherds need 90–120 minutes of exercise daily, including both physical and mental stimulation.
Their double coat requires brushing 2–3 times per week; they shed year-round and heavily in spring/fall.
They are prone to degenerative myelopathy and hip dysplasia — regular vet monitoring is important.
Mental stimulation (obedience training, puzzle toys, scent work) is as important as physical exercise.
Their ears should be checked weekly for signs of infection or debris.
High-quality protein diet is important to maintain muscle mass and coat health.
poodle: Poodles (standard) need 40–60 minutes of daily exercise; miniature and toy poodles need 20–40 minutes.
Their curly coat does not shed much but requires professional grooming every 6–8 weeks to prevent matting.
Daily brushing is recommended to prevent tangles between grooming appointments.
Poodles are highly intelligent and need daily mental stimulation — training sessions double as enrichment.
Ear cleaning is important as their floppy ears and hair inside the ear canal can cause infections.
Poodles are generally healthy but can be prone to Addison's disease — regular vet checkups are key.
beagle: Beagles need at least 60 minutes of exercise daily — they are scent-driven and love to explore.
They should always be kept on a leash or in a fenced area as their nose can override recall instincts.
Beagles are prone to obesity — meals should be measured and treats limited.
Their floppy ears need weekly cleaning to prevent moisture buildup and infections.
Beagles are vocal dogs — enrichment activities help reduce excessive barking from boredom.
Their short coat needs only weekly brushing; they are moderate shedders.
shiba inu: Shiba Inus need 40–60 minutes of vigorous exercise daily.
They have a thick double coat that requires brushing 2–3 times per week; they blow their coat seasonally.
Shiba Inus are independent and can be escape artists — ensure all outdoor areas are securely fenced.
They are generally clean dogs and do well with grooming routines.
Early socialization is important as Shibas can be reserved around strangers.
Mental enrichment such as puzzle feeders and short training sessions helps channel their intelligence.

general: Cats need a clean litter box scooped at least once daily; a dirty box can cause behavioral issues.
Annual vet visits are recommended for healthy adult cats; senior cats (10+) benefit from biannual visits.
Cats benefit from environmental enrichment: climbing structures, window perches, and puzzle feeders.
Fresh water should always be available; many cats prefer running water (a fountain can increase intake).
Indoor cats need regular playtime to stay mentally and physically healthy — at least 15–20 minutes daily.
Dental disease is common in cats — aim to brush teeth several times per week.
persian: Persian cats require daily coat brushing to prevent severe matting — this is non-negotiable.
Their flat (brachycephalic) face makes them prone to respiratory issues and eye discharge — monitor breathing.
Eye discharge should be cleaned gently with a damp cloth every day to prevent staining and infection.
Persian cats are lower-energy and suited to indoor living; light play sessions of 10–15 minutes are ideal.
Their facial folds should be cleaned weekly to prevent skin irritation.
Persians are prone to polycystic kidney disease (PKD) — genetic testing and regular kidney panels are recommended.
siamese: Siamese cats are highly social and vocal — they need daily interaction and dislike being left alone for long periods.
They are active and playful; two sessions of interactive play per day (10–15 min each) are recommended.
Their short coat requires minimal grooming — a weekly brush is sufficient.
Siamese are prone to dental issues — regular teeth brushing is important.
They can be prone to respiratory infections due to their elongated facial structure — monitor for sneezing.
Environmental enrichment (toys, cat trees, puzzles) is essential for this intelligent breed.
maine coon: Maine Coons have a semi-long coat that requires brushing 2–3 times per week to prevent tangles.
They are one of the largest domestic cat breeds — ensure food portions are calibrated to weight.
Maine Coons are playful and dog-like; daily interactive play sessions of 20–30 minutes are ideal.
They are prone to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) — regular cardiac screenings are recommended.
Their tufted paws may collect debris — check and clean paws weekly.
Maine Coons enjoy water and may drink from faucets; a water fountain encourages good hydration.
british shorthair: British Shorthairs have a dense plush coat that benefits from brushing 1–2 times per week.
They are calm and adaptable cats; moderate daily play of 15–20 minutes keeps them fit.
British Shorthairs are prone to obesity — monitor food intake carefully and avoid free feeding.
They can be prone to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy — vet screenings are advisable.
Their calm temperament makes them good candidates for indoor-only living.
Regular nail trimming every 2–3 weeks is recommended as they tend to be less active scratchers.
